An Introduction to Chinese Ancient Philosophy - XIan Qin Philosophy

Eastern Zhou (ca. 771-256 BCE) Dynasty includes two periods: Spring and Autumn Period (770-ca. 475 BCE) and Warring States Period (ca. 475-221 BCE). During the first time frame, there were hundreds of small kingdoms in current Chinese territory since Zhou's feudal aristocracy. Big Kingdom planned to conquer smaller ones, while smaller ones tried to maintain their independence; so all kingdoms were seeking "change" for their own benefits. Due to the strong need of new ideology/institution and the variously dynamic territorial politics, there were many brilliant thinkers, philosophers and politicians. Their masterpieces generated profound and endless impact on Chinese culture. There are different type of theories, such as:

Theory Book Founder Glorious Heir
Daoism Lao Zi, Zhuang Zi Lao Zi Zhuang Zi
Confucianism Lun Yu, Meng Zi Confucius Meng Zi
Legalism Han Fei Zi Han Fei Shang Yang
Mohism Mo Zi Mo Di N/A

etc

  • FYI: "Zi" (“子”), in Ancient China, is a glorious suffix for respected intellectuals. Every Ancient Chinese, who is called "Zi", is considered to be great thinker in Chinese history.

This period of time is my favorite, because of freedom, diversity and dynamic. Afterword, at end of Warring States period, Qin Kingdom utilized Legalism to unify the whole China to form Qin Dynasty. However, the Legalism emphasized on strict and cruel law, which did not work out for reigning a giant ancient emperor. Then the famous Han Dynasty rose on the debris of Qin Dynasty. Han Wu Di（141-86 BCE）, who is an important Emperor, nominated a Confucian disciple - Dong, Zhongshu - to be the Minister. Dong esteemed Confucianism， abolishing all other philosophy. Dong organized a group of Confucians to distort original Confucianism to build dictatorship, hierarchy and bureaucracy. Then Confucianism has been dominant in China for almost two thousand years until People Republic China.
